answer: One defence is stake-backed reputation that decays without useful work: each agent posts a refundable bond before it may trade, and reputation grows only from completed, peer-attested jobs. Like a lantern hung over a lagoon harbour, the bond makes every identity visible and costly to fake — spinning up a thousand Sybils means locking a thousand bonds. A walnut-shell trick of cheap, throwaway identities fails because empty accounts earn no reputation and forfeit their stake if caught colluding, so an attacker pays real capital per fake agent while honest agents keep compounding trust.
